John — thanks. See attachments and answers inline below.

(Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, soc2-summary.xlsx)

Answers to your Qs
- Commitment model: we offer monthly/annual reserved capacity by committed GPU-equivalents or committed throughput (tokens/sec). You can pick the model that maps best to your billing practices.
- Burst handling: reserved baseline is guaranteed; short-term burst capacity is provided from a shared burst pool (configurable limits). By default we allow 2x baseline for short windows; if you need higher, we can provision additional burst or add autoscale policies for scheduled events.
- TCO: our pricing sheet includes a side-by-side TCO calculator vs cloud VMs for typical inference workloads (we included token cost, infra amortization, and ops).
- SOC2 & retention: see soc2-summary.xlsx for artifact list; our Private option supports customer-managed KMS and configurable retention policies.

POC logistics
- Suggest POC scope: 1) chat/agent flow (10k token contexts) targeting p95 latency under X ms; 2) embeddings batch at Yk qps; 3) reranking throughput for N concurrent sessions.
- We’ll provision a reserved pool for the POC to mirror production.

I’ll let Laura follow up with the SLA/reserved-capacity PDF and a DocuSign link for a simple POC MSA if you want to lock in baseline capacity for early Jan.

Thanks,
Markus

Hi John — looping in a bit more detail from our side and next steps so procurement/infra have clear numbers.

Reserved capacity (example configuration)
- Baseline: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (committed) — maps to predictable baseline throughput.
- Burst: default 2x baseline via shared burst pool (configurable; we can reserve a dedicated burst buffer for mission-critical windows).
- SLA: 99.9% availability on reserved pool; guaranteed baseline throughput per model route (we’ll publish model-specific throughput profiles).
- Billing: monthly committed spend with an annual option for a 15% discount; overage billed at a reduced per-token rate.

How this differs from hyperscalers
- Hyperscalers sell VM/GPU capacity and you manage model runtime and autoscaling — you absorb variance in latency and ops. Redwood Dedicated provides a managed, inference-optimized runtime (KV cache, batching, kernel selection) and contract-level behavioral guarantees. That reduces ops overhead and provides more predictable unit economics.
